role.en: Filipino physician and propagandist; financed the first printing of Noli Me Tangere
role.fil: Pilipinong manggagamot at propagandista; tumustos sa unang paglilimbag ng Noli Me Tangere
role.de: Philippinischer Arzt und Propagandist; finanzierte den ersten Druck des Noli Me Tangere

portrait.alt: Grainy head-and-shoulders photograph of a young Maximo Viola in a dark jacket and high collar

quote.en: I am celebrating Christmas, together with my compatriot from Barcelona, the physician Dr. Maximo Viola; I asked to purchase chicken, beer, and many others… I have always celebrated this day since I came here to Europe, sometimes with my fellow countrymen, sometimes in solitude; I do not regret spending the little that I have to celebrate this day.
quote.fil: Nagdiriwang ako ng Pasko kasama ang aking kababayan mula Barcelona, ang manggagamot na si Dr. Maximo Viola; ipinabili ko ng manok, serbesa, at marami pang iba… Lagi kong idinidiwang ang araw na ito mula nang pumarito ako sa Europa, kung minsan kasama ang aking mga kababayan, kung minsan sa pag-iisa; hindi ko pinagsisisihan ang paggasta ng kakaunting taglay ko upang idiwang ang araw na ito.
quote.de: Ich feiere Weihnachten zusammen mit meinem Landsmann aus Barcelona, dem Arzt Dr. Maximo Viola; ich ließ Hühner, Bier und vieles andere besorgen… Diesen Tag habe ich stets gefeiert, seit ich nach Europa kam, manchmal mit meinen Landsleuten, manchmal in Einsamkeit; ich bereue nicht, das Wenige, das ich habe, für diesen Tag auszugeben.

quoteSource.en: Rizal to Doña Teodora Alonzo, Berlin, 25 December 1886
quoteSource.fil: Rizal kay Doña Teodora Alonzo, Berlin, 25 Disyembre 1886
quoteSource.de: Rizal an Doña Teodora Alonzo, Berlin, 25. Dezember 1886

bio.en:
Without this person, would we even come to read and learn about Noli Me Tangere more than a century after the book was written? Dr. Maximo Viola was instrumental in cementing Rizal's legacy in Filipino history and literature, giving Rizal the financial means to print and publish the Noli Me Tangere after its completion in 1887.

Born to Pedro Viola and Isabel Sison in the town of Sta. Rita, in the province of Bulacan, Viola studied pre-medicine at the University of Santo Tomas and pursued further studies at the University of Barcelona, graduating in 1882. Having almost similar educational backgrounds and being members of the Propaganda Movement in Europe, Rizal and Viola became friends.

Viola later on visited him in Berlin when Rizal was in a dire state during the writing of Noli Me Tangere in February 1887. Upon learning that Rizal was living on meager means just to finish his novel, Viola offered to loan Rizal the sum needed to initially publish 2,000 copies of the Noli that would later stir the anger of the Spanish authorities. In gratitude, Rizal gave Viola a galley proof and copy of the book, making him one of the first to read the Noli Me Tangere among the probably hundreds of thousands that were able to read the book until this day.

Rizal found a compatriot and a travel companion in Viola. After the publication of the Noli, Rizal was free to take on Viola's invitation to visit European cities with him. Leaving Berlin on 11 May 1887, Rizal and Viola would stop at cities in Germany, the Czech Republic, Switzerland, and Austria. This cosmopolitan sojourn in Europe helped Rizal meet notable key figures in the field of anthropology and ophthalmology, and in finally meeting Ferdinand Blumentritt, with whom he already had an established friendship through their correspondences. In their stop in Dresden, Rizal would also be fascinated by the ethnological collections and zoological specimens, which would perhaps influence his actions of sending objects and collections representing the different cultural groups in the Philippines.

Marseille, France was Rizal's last stop in Europe before he boarded the steamer Djemnah on 3 July 1887, crossing the Mediterranean Sea and the Indian Ocean through the Suez Canal to get to Saigon (now Ho Chi Minh), Vietnam. Here, Rizal would board another steamer, the Hai Phong, which would bring him back to Manila on 5 August 1887. That same year, Viola would also return to the Philippines to practice medicine. They were now home.
bio.fil:
Kung wala ang taong ito, mababasa at mapag-aaralan kaya natin ang Noli Me Tangere mahigit isang dantaon matapos isulat ang aklat? Naging mahalaga si Dr. Maximo Viola sa pagtitibay ng pamana ni Rizal sa kasaysayan at panitikang Pilipino, sa pagbibigay kay Rizal ng kakayahang pinansiyal upang ilimbag at ilathala ang Noli Me Tangere matapos itong matapos noong 1887.

Isinilang kay Pedro Viola at Isabel Sison sa bayan ng Sta. Rita, sa lalawigan ng Bulacan, nag-aral si Viola ng premedisina sa Unibersidad ng Santo Tomas at nagpatuloy ng pag-aaral sa Unibersidad ng Barcelona, at nagtapos noong 1882. Dahil sa halos katulad na pinagmulang edukasyonal at sa pagiging kasapi ng Kilusang Propaganda sa Europa, naging magkaibigan si Rizal at Viola.

Kalaunan ay dumalaw siya kay Rizal sa Berlin noong nasa mahigpit na kalagayan ito sa panahon ng pagsusulat ng Noli Me Tangere noong Pebrero 1887. Sa pagkaalam na namumuhay si Rizal sa kakarampot na kabuhayan upang matapos ang kanyang nobela, iniharap ni Viola ang pagpapautang kay Rizal ng salaping kailangan upang maunang mailathala ang 2,000 sipi ng Noli na kalaunan ay magpapagalit sa mga awtoridad na Espanyol. Sa pasasalamat, ibinigay ni Rizal kay Viola ang isang galley proof at sipi ng aklat, na naging dahilan upang siya ang isa sa mga kauna-unahang nakabasa ng Noli Me Tangere sa marahil ay daan-daang libong nakabasa ng aklat hanggang sa araw na ito.

Natagpuan ni Rizal sa kay Viola ang isang kababayan at kasama sa paglalakbay. Matapos mailathala ang Noli, malaya nang matanggap ni Rizal ang paanyaya ni Viola na dalawin ang mga lungsod ng Europa kasama nito. Umalis sa Berlin noong ika-11 ng Mayo 1887, huminto si Rizal at Viola sa mga lungsod sa Alemanya, Republikang Tseko, Switzerland, at Austria. Ang kosmopolitanong paglalakbay na ito sa Europa ang tumulong kay Rizal upang makilala ang mga mahalagang tao sa larangan ng antropolohiya at optalmolohiya, at upang tuluyan nang makilala si Ferdinand Blumentritt, na may nabuo na niyang pagkakaibigan sa pamamagitan ng kanilang sulatan. Sa kanilang pagtigil sa Dresden, mahahalina rin si Rizal sa mga koleksiyong etnolohiko at ispesimeng soolohiko, na marahil ay nakaimpluwensiya sa kanyang mga hakbang ng pagpapadala ng mga bagay at koleksiyong kumakatawan sa iba't ibang pangkat kultural sa Pilipinas.

Ang Marseille, Pransiya ang huling hinintuan ni Rizal sa Europa bago siya sumakay sa bapor na Djemnah noong ika-3 ng Hulyo 1887, sa pagtawid sa Dagat Mediteraneo at Karagatang Indiyano sa pamamagitan ng Kanal Suez upang makarating sa Saigon (ngayon ay Ho Chi Minh), Vietnam. Dito, sasakay si Rizal sa ibang bapor, ang Hai Phong, na magbabalik sa kanya sa Maynila noong ika-5 ng Agosto 1887. Sa taon ding iyon, magbabalik din si Viola sa Pilipinas upang magpraktis ng medisina. Nasa tahanan na sila.
bio.de:
Ohne diesen Mann – würden wir das Noli Me Tangere mehr als ein Jahrhundert nach seiner Entstehung überhaupt lesen und kennen? Dr. Maximo Viola trug entscheidend dazu bei, Rizals Platz in der philippinischen Geschichte und Literatur zu sichern, indem er ihm die Mittel verschaffte, das 1887 vollendete Noli Me Tangere zu drucken und herauszugeben.

Als Sohn von Pedro Viola und Isabel Sison in der Gemeinde Sta. Rita in der Provinz Bulacan geboren, studierte Viola Vormedizin an der Universität Santo Tomas und setzte seine Studien an der Universität Barcelona fort, wo er 1882 abschloss. Wegen ihrer nahezu gleichen Bildungswege und ihrer Mitgliedschaft in der Propagandabewegung in Europa wurden Rizal und Viola Freunde.

Später besuchte er Rizal in Berlin, als dieser sich im Februar 1887 beim Schreiben des Noli Me Tangere in bedrängter Lage befand. Als er erfuhr, dass Rizal in größter Kargheit lebte, nur um seinen Roman zu vollenden, bot Viola ihm die Summe als Darlehen an, die für den ersten Druck von 2.000 Exemplaren des Noli nötig war – jenes Buches, das später den Zorn der spanischen Behörden erregte. Aus Dankbarkeit schenkte Rizal Viola einen Korrekturabzug und ein Exemplar des Buches und machte ihn damit zu einem der Ersten, die das Noli Me Tangere lasen, unter den wohl Hunderttausenden, die es bis heute gelesen haben.

In Viola fand Rizal einen Landsmann und Reisegefährten. Nach dem Erscheinen des Noli konnte Rizal Violas Einladung annehmen, mit ihm europäische Städte zu besuchen. Am 11. Mai 1887 brachen Rizal und Viola von Berlin auf und machten Station in Städten Deutschlands, der heutigen Tschechischen Republik, der Schweiz und Österreichs. Diese weltläufige Reise durch Europa half Rizal, bedeutende Persönlichkeiten der Anthropologie und der Augenheilkunde kennenzulernen und schließlich Ferdinand Blumentritt persönlich zu begegnen, mit dem ihn durch den Briefwechsel längst eine Freundschaft verband. Bei ihrem Aufenthalt in Dresden war Rizal überdies von den ethnologischen Sammlungen und zoologischen Präparaten fasziniert, was vielleicht sein späteres Handeln beeinflusste, Objekte und Sammlungen zu senden, die die verschiedenen Kulturgruppen der Philippinen vertreten.

Marseille in Frankreich war Rizals letzte Station in Europa, bevor er am 3. Juli 1887 den Dampfer Djemnah bestieg und über das Mittelmeer und den Indischen Ozean durch den Suezkanal nach Saigon (heute Ho-Chi-Minh-Stadt) in Vietnam fuhr. Dort ging er auf einen anderen Dampfer, die Hai Phong, die ihn am 5. August 1887 nach Manila zurückbrachte. Im selben Jahr kehrte auch Viola auf die Philippinen zurück, um als Arzt zu praktizieren. Nun waren sie zu Hause.
